dimensions.assessment: Applies locally to Gateway Arch National Park in St. Louis, Missouri, the National Park Service, and the Gateway Arch Park Foundation.
dimensions.evidence: The Foundation, a nonprofit organization that serves as the official philanthropic partner of the Park.

dimensions.assessment: Allows private events in park buildings under specified conditions designed to prevent disruption to public use.
dimensions.evidence: shall not take place during times or in locations that prevent or disrupt public use or access to the Park or Park buildings.

dimensions.assessment: Requires the NPS to charge fees and recover all costs incurred for maintenance, utilities, administrative expenses, security, and personnel.
dimensions.evidence: may recover all costs incurred as a result of the private events and use of the Park and Park buildings, including maintenance, utilities, administrative expenses, security, and personnel costs.

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes a specific pilot agreement and reporting requirements without broader structural statutory changes.
dimensions.evidence: may enter into a one-time agreement for a period not to exceed five years with the Foundation to host private events at the Park

dimensions.assessment: Temporary authority limited to a five-year agreement, with a complete sunset on the authority and existing agreements seven years after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The authority to enter into and carry out an agreement with the Foundation pursuant to this Act shall sunset on the date that is 7 years after the date of enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Exact dollar amounts for fees collected or costs recovered
importance_detail.rationale: This bill authorizes a one-time, five-year agreement (with a seven-year sunset) for the National Park Service to allow the Gateway Arch Park Foundation to host private events at Gateway Arch National Park buildings in St. Louis, Missouri. The NPS must recover all associated costs and charge a fee for wear and tear.
